questions.question_text:
In a class of 30, the ratio of girls to boys is $2:3$.
How many boys are in the class?

options.why: Uses the number of girls ratio parts instead of the boys parts.
Uses the ratio number without scaling it to a total of 30.
Splits the class into two equal groups instead of five ratio parts.

questions.solution_text: There are $2+3=5$ equal parts, so each part is $30/5=6$. Boys make up three parts: $3\times6=18$.

questions.question_text:
Riley shares some money with his brother in the ratio $4:3$.
If Riley gets £28, how much does his brother get?

options.why: This uses a smaller value than the three parts belonging to Riley's brother.
This multiplies the ratio parts incorrectly after finding Riley's share.
This multiplies £28 by a ratio number instead of finding one part.

questions.solution_text: Riley's 4 parts equal £28, so 1 part is $28\div4=£7$. His brother receives 3 parts: $3\times£7=£21$.

questions.question_text:
Adam and Matt share some money in the ratio 4 : 9.
Adam gets £468.
Which of these is the total amount of money shared?

options.why: The ratio parts have not been used to calculate the complete total.
This calculates Matt's share rather than the total amount shared.
The value does not account correctly for all 13 ratio parts.

questions.solution_text:
Four parts are £468, so one part is $468 \div 4 = 117$.
There are $13$ parts altogether.
Total $= 13 \times 117$
$= 1521$
The amount is £1521.
